text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
SIR JOHN EARDLEY-WILMOT, who became Governor of Van Dieman's Land, (Tasmania) was born on this day in 1783.
Scottish explorer WILLIAM LANDSBOROUGH, who crossed Australia from North to South searching for BOURKE and WILLS, was born in 1825.
British Doctor JOSEPH BANCROFT, who experimented with Australian native plants, was born in 1836. His Brisbane home was called KELVIN GROVE, which eventually lent its name to the suburb.
Australian artist FRED McCUBBIN was born in 1855.
Australian surveyor ALFRED CANNING, who founded the CANNING STOCKROUTE from the Kimberleys to the Goldfields, was born in 1860.
American actress ANNE SHERIDAN was born on this day in 1915.
Australian athlete RON CLARKE was born in 1937.

US guitarist, keyboard player, songwriter and singer JERRY HARRISON was born in 1949. He was a member of 'Modern Lovers' for four years in the seventies and then joined 'Talking Heads'. In 1988 he released his solo album "Casual Gods".
** EVENTS **
1613 : MICHAEL ROMANOV was elected Tsar of Russia,
beginning the Romanov rule in Russia.
1741 : JETHRO TULL, English agriculturalist, died. He
invented the seed drill and pioneered the planting of seeds in rows.
1842 : The first sewing-machine was patented by JOHN
GREENOUGH.
1849 : In the second British-Sikh war, the British
inflicted a huge defeat on a force of 50,000 Sikhs under SHIR SINGH at the battle of Gujerat.
1858 : The first electric burglar alarm was installed at
the home of BOSTON man, EDWIN HOLMES.
1905 : Thirty-five cars and motor cycles set out on the
Sydney to Melbourne reliability race.
1918 : The Australian Light Horse captured the city of
Jericho in Jordan.
1941 : Japan warned Britain against military movements in
South-East Asia. By the end of the year Japan had invaded Malaya and landed in the Phillipines.
1952 : American actress ELIZABETH TAYLOR married hotel
magnate CONRAD HILTON Junior.
1960 : President FIDEL CASTRO nationalised all private
businesses in Cuba.
1963 : The Soviet Union threatened a
World War if the United States launched any attack on Cuba.
1965 : American Muslim activist MALCOLM X was shot dead
in New York.
1972 : President RICHARD NIXON became the first U.S.
President to visit China.
1980 : 13 people were killed in a light plane crash at
Sydney Airport.
1986 : The world's oldest man (to-date), 120 year-old
SHIGECHIYO IZUMI of Japan, died.
1989 : Two members of WINNIE MANDELA's bodyguard were
charged with murdering 14 year-old STOMPIE MOCKETSI.
1991 : The epitome of the prima ballerina Dame MARGOT

FONTEYN died at the age of 73. Her interpretation of the classic ballet roles established her as one of the century's foremost dancers. She started her career with the London Sadler's Wells company in 1934 and soon became their lead ballerina. Her legendary partnership with RUDOLPH NUREYEV began in 1962. She was 43. In 1955 she married Panama's ambassador ROBERTO ARIAS, who was paralysed ten years later in an assassination attempt.
FONTEYN devoted herself to caring for her husband. On her 60th birthday she was named prima ballerina assolutta by the Imperial Russian Ballet.
1996 : JEANNE CALMENT, believed to be the world's oldest
person, celebrated her 121st birthday with memories ranging from meeting Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh to her new career as a pop star.
